text: Problem set 1 Problem 1. Let V be the set of positive continuous functions f : R → (0, ∞) equipped with the addition: (f + g)(x) = f (x)g(x) (multiplying the functions f and g) and scalar multiplication (cf )(x) = f (x) c (f raised to the c power). Show that V is a vector space over R by finding the additive identity and additive inverse and checking the axioms. Problem 2. Let S be the set of polynomials of degree exactly n i.e. S = {antn+· · ·+a0 ∈ Pn(F ) : an ̸= 0}. Is S a subspace of Pn(F )? Justify your answer. Problem 3. To make a distinction, we write the zero vector as ⃗0 and the 0 scalar as 0. Use the axioms of vector spaces as well as Proposition 1.3 (vii) proved in class to show the following: (i) The element ⃗0 ∈ V is unique. (ii) For any x ∈ V , 0x = ⃗0. (iii) For any a ∈ F , a⃗0 = ⃗0. (iv) If a ∈ F , x ∈ V such that ax = ⃗0, then either a = 0 (in F ) or x = ⃗0 (in V ). (v) For any x ∈ V , the element −x is unique. (vi) For any x ∈ V , (−1)x = −x. Hint for (ii), (iii): write 0x = (0 + 0)x and a⃗0 = a(⃗0 + ⃗0). Problem 4. This problem is to introduce the set of complex numbers C. A complex number is a number of the form a + bi where a, b ∈ R and i is the imaginary number satisfying the property i2 = −1. The number a is called the real part and b is called the imaginary part. A complex number a + bi is 0 if and only if a = b = 0.1 The addition of complex numbers is defined as (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i. The multiplication of two complex numbers is defined as (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac − bd) + (ad + bc)i.
